=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/security_pass_skip.py: lines 190-194 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `"ai:workflow-heal" in candidates` block at line 193 and the associated comment at lines 190-192 are unreachable dead code.
  WHY: Line 187 builds `candidates` from `SKIP_LABEL_MARKERS`, which after this PR contains only `"ai:security"`. The expression `"ai:workflow-heal" in candidates` is always False. It does not cause incorrect execution, but is a maintainability defect.
- changelog.d/6118-ci-failure-triage-workflow-run.md: line 12 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: States "release-workflow heal issues retain their existing exemption", which directly contradicts the implementation that removed `ai:workflow-heal` from `SKIP_LABEL_MARKERS`.
  WHY: All heal fix PRs into the default branch now require a security audit, while operators reading this changelog may believe release-workflow heal issues bypass the audit.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The link ed issue (issue #6486) and auto-decision AD-1 require removing `ai:workflow-heal` from `SKIP_LABEL_MARKERS` so no workflow-heal issue of any kind skips the security pass. Every documentation source must reflect that release-workflow heal issues no longer have an exemption.
  Expected change site: changelog.d/6118-ci-failure-triage-workflow-run.md line 12
  Evidence of absence: The line "release-workflow heal issues retain their existing exemption" is the last-run artifact from the narrower CI-only-exemption scope. The PR removes `ai:workflow-heal` from `SKIP_LABEL_MARKERS` entirely, so NO heal issue skips the pass. The README.md and agents.md texts were correctly updated to say all heal fix PRs require an audit; this changelog fragment was not.
  SEVERITY: high
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/security_pass_skip.py: line 68 (definition), line 187-194 (caller), line 238-240 (caller) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: CI_HEAL_CONTEXT_RE and the two consumer checks are unreachable dead code.
  WHY: `candidates` can only contain `"ai:security"`, making the line 193 check permanently False; in `check_issue`, the first sub-expression of the OR at line 238 short-circuits True for workflow-heal-only issues, making the line 240 check unreachable. The dead code misleads maintainers about an existing CI-only exemption.
- tests/test_security_pass_skip.py: lines 103-108 (`test_ci_workflow_heal_does_not_skip_security_pass`) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The test name asserts a CI-context-driven rejection, but the rejection comes from `decide_security_pass_skip` returning `"ai:security: body has no ai:security automation marker"`.
  WHY: The workflow line and workflow-heal label are irrelevant to the rejection path, so the test would pass without CI context and would not catch a regression that restores an exemption for non-CI heal sources.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The linked issue body requires "Require the security pass for CI-derived workflow-heal fixes; scope any exemption to a verified producer and source-run provenance, not the issue label alone." The auto-decision AD-1 selected Option A, which removes `ai:workflow-heal` from `SKIP_LABEL_MARKERS` entirely (matching the `ai:check-triage` precedent) — i.e. no `ai:workflow-heal` exemption of any kind.
  Expected change site: changelog.d/6118-ci-failure-triage-workflow-run.md line 12 (operator-facing paragraph).
  Evidence of absence: The line still reads "A fix PR for a CI-derived heal issue must pass the head-bound security audit; release-workflow heal issues retain their existing exemption." With Option A, the proven exemption is gone — every `ai:workflow-heal` fix PR is now rejected by `decide_security_pass_skip` with `"reason": "no skip label"`, including release-workflow heal issues. The PR's own `README.md` (lines 1563-1565), `agents.md` (lines 218-220), `changelog.d/6486-workflow-heal-security-pass.md`, and `scripts/security_pass_skip.py` all describe the broader scope. `changelog.d/6118-ci-failure-triage-workflow-run.md` line 12 is the only documentation source that still claims the narrower scope with a release-workflow exemption, contradicting both the implementation and every other doc source.
  SEVERITY: high
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
